answer.text:
**How to Create a Texas Tech K-12 Parent Portal Account**

To create a Parent Portal account for Texas Tech K-12, follow these steps:

**Step-by-Step Instructions:**

- Go to the Parent Portal Registration page (opens in new tab).
- Click on "I do not have an Account Registered on the Parent Portal but would like to Create One."
- Enter your First Name, Last Name, and a unique email address (the email must not be the same as your student’s email).
- Create a password that meets these requirements:
  - At least 12 characters long
  - Includes upper and lower-case letters
  - Has at least one number
  - Has at least one special character
- After entering your information, you’ll be directed to the "Students" page.
- You can connect to an existing student by selecting "I would like to Add a Child who is already enrolled" and entering their student ID and date of birth.
- If you want to apply for enrollment for a new child, select "I would like to Apply For Enrollment for a new child" and complete the application.

**Important Notes:**

- Each parent/guardian and student must have a unique email address.
- If your student already has an account, have their matriculation number and date of birth ready to link accounts.

**Need Help?**

- Call Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877
- Email: ttuk12@ttu.edu

Step 1: Attendance is based on progress in your child’s courses.

Step 2: Your child must complete 5% of each course's assignments each week. For example, if a course has 20 assignments, at least one should be completed each week.

Step 3: Courses must be completed within the designated tuition free program semester timeline.

Step 4: Students must stay enrolled in at least four courses.

Supplemental Program Information

Anyone looking to supplement their current school curriculum or home school curriculum can enroll in Texas Tech K-12.  Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Each course has lessons, which are like chapters, and a final exam. The final exam will be proctored online by an online proctoring service.

Characteristics Related to Potential Giftedness

Step 4: Student’s use of quantitative expressions and quantitative reasoning. An example to illustrate this comes from the writer’s experience in observing a kindergarten class where the students were playing a game in which each round resulted in the elimination of one child. After the game had progressed for several rounds, the teacher asked the children, “Are there more girls left in the game or more boys?” One child responded, “There are only one-half as many boys left as girls.” Not only was the response correct, it was also a highly unusual quantitative response for a kindergarten child to make. Some children exhibit the ability to translate rather lengthy, sometimes complex, verbal material into quantitative terms. The ability to do this kind of translation requires a level of abstraction and facility with quantitative expression that is important to identify.

Step 5: Student’s ability to devise or adopt a systematic strategy for solving problems and to change the strategy if it is not working. This ability discriminates between excellent problem-solvers and average problem-solvers. Children who are exceptional in cognitive development tend to have mastery of a large number of strategies for attacking novel or difficult problems and tend to be able to evaluate the effectiveness of the strategy as they work on the problems and change strategies when the one they are using does not appear to be working. Other children either have no systematic strategy or only one strategy, which they persist in using, even though it should be apparent to them that it is not working.

Step 6: Special skills students exhibit that are unusual for their age or grade. The first five categories listed relate primarily to verbal, quantitative, or problem-solving skills. However, an observant teacher, parent, or other adult may notice children doing other kinds of things that are quite unusual for their age or grade. For example, the writer saw a first-grade child during a free activity period drawing in perspective, which is quite unusual for a child that age. There are numerous opportunities to observe such things as skill in expressive movement, artistry in mimicry or dramatizations, and originality in design or model building or art.

Grade Level Placement for Transfer Students

If you transfer to Texas Tech Middle School from an accredited public or private school, you will be placed using the grade level indicated by your previous school. You must provide an official transcript or report card for placement.

Enrollment Requirements

You will need to submit the following documents for your application to be processed:

Step 1: Birth Certificate

Step 2: Proof of Texas Residency

Step 3: Unofficial Transcript

For homeschool students, please also provide a transcript and be prepared to take Credit By Exams (CBE) for grade placement.

For homeschool students, please also provide a transcript and be prepared to take Credit By Exams (CBE) for grade placement.

Characteristics Related to Potential Giftedness

There are certain student characteristics related to potential giftedness that can be more reliably appraised by teachers, parents, and others who have extended opportunities to observe students than by tests or formal instruments. Some of the more important ones are:

Step 1: Student’s use of language. This includes such things as range of vocabulary, precision in the use of words, and complexity of sentence structure. Although these can be appraised in a test situation, one obtains a better appraisal of the level of habitual use of language through observation in a wide variety of everyday situations.

Step 2: Quality of students’ questions. Most children ask questions, and some children ask many questions. Although it is true that bright children typically ask many questions, it is the quality rather than the number of questions that discriminates most sharply between the potentially gifted child and other children. One wants to look at the unusualness of a question in relation to age or grade or the insightfulness of a question, i.e., indications that the individual has grasped the central nature of the phenomenon, or indications that the individual is relating the present task or situation to other experience.

Step 3: Quality of examples, illustrations, or elaborations that a student used in explaining something or in describing events or in telling stories. Not only do exceptional students have a good command of language, but they also tend to use examples that are apt and original or to produce unusual analogies to illustrate points. Some students show an unusual ability to translate verbal materials into pictorial modes or models or schematic diagrams. All these behaviors indicate a high level of understanding of the material that the students are using, ability to communicate ideas, and originality.

**Homeschool Transcripts for Texas Tech K-12 Enrollment**

If your child has never attended public school and you are homeschooling, here’s what you need to know about transcripts for Texas Tech K-12:

**For Enrollment:**
- You will need to provide a homeschool transcript when applying to Texas Tech K-12.
- The transcript should list all courses your child has completed, grades earned, and the academic years for each course.
- You, as the parent/educator, can create and sign this transcript.

**Important for High School Credit:**
- Grades on homeschool transcripts and transcripts from non-accredited schools are **not transferable** for credit at Texas Tech K-12.
- To receive credit for non-accredited (homeschool) courses, your child must take Credit by Exams (CBEs) or enroll in the courses through Texas Tech K-12.

**Credit by Exam (CBE) Option:**
- Students can demonstrate proficiency and earn credit by passing a Texas Tech K-12 CBE with a minimum score of 80% (for no prior instruction).
- For high school, a CBE score of 80%+ is required for credit if there was no prior instruction.

**Next Steps:**
- Prepare a homeschool transcript for the application.
- Be ready for your child to take CBEs for grade placement and credit, especially for high school level courses.
- For more information or help with the process, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Is this school a good fit for a student with special needs?

This is the parent’s decision.  Of course, you know your child best and you are the best person to determine the environment in which your child will experience the most success.

Many students with special needs do very well in our online program. Some of these needs that are readily accommodated include:  use of a screen reader, need larger font, need highlighting or color change functionality, need a learning environment free from distractions, need extended time on exams, have social anxiety, have medical concerns. Our online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 federal web compliance requirements.

Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

Texas Tech K-12 is a statewide online school district and does not have a physical campus nor a geographic service district. We serve full-time students from across the entire state of Texas.

We have special education personnel to ensure and monitor appropriate accommodations identified in the Individualized Education Program or 504 plan. We closely monitor the academic progress of all students and will provide appropriate interventions and services as identified.

**Requirements and Tips for Being a Learning Coach with Texas Tech K-12**

**Learning Coach Requirements:**
- **Role:** The Learning Coach is typically a parent/guardian or responsible adult who supports the student’s learning at home.
- **Responsibilities:**
  - Monitor student progress and lesson mastery.
  - Review student work.
  - Communicate with teachers as needed.
  - Help establish a daily routine and ensure regular attendance (minimum 3 days per week, with at least 5% of course assignments completed each week).
- **Technical Requirements:**
  - Access to a computer that meets minimum technology requirements.
  - Reliable, high-speed internet access.

**What the Student Needs to Be Successful:**

- **Technology:**
  - Modern computer (≤5 years old) with webcam, microphone, speakers, and updated antivirus software.
  - Operating System: Windows 10+, macOS 11+, Chrome OS, or Linux (Ubuntu 18.04+).
  - Supported browsers: Latest versions of Google Chrome (required for online exams), Firefox, Edge, or Safari (macOS only).
  - Broadband internet (at least 1.5 Mbps, wired preferred).
  - JavaScript, cookies, and pop-ups enabled; ad blockers disabled.
  - PDF reader (e.g., Adobe Acrobat Reader).

- **School Supplies:**
  - General supplies: spiral notebooks, pens, pencils, highlighters.
  - Graphing calculator (for certain math courses).
  - Household supplies for specialty courses (art, science, etc.).

- **Academic Success Tips:**
  - Establish a consistent daily routine for coursework.
  - Set aside specific hours each day for schoolwork.
  - Use an academic calendar to track assignments and exams.
  - Read and follow all course instructions and syllabi.
  - Communicate regularly with teachers via course messaging.
  - Maintain satisfactory progress in all courses.
  - Participate in required state testing (STAAR/EOC) if in the tuition-free program.

- **Time Management:**
  - Students should log in to the portal within the first two days of enrolling.
  - Work in courses regularly and avoid falling behind.
  - Plan ahead for assignment grading times (teachers have up to two business days to grade assignments).

**Additional Notes:**
- The Learning Coach is essential for younger students and those new to online learning.
- The program is asynchronous—students work at their own pace, but must meet weekly progress requirements.
- For students with special needs, ensure the ARD or 504 committee agrees the online program is appropriate.

**Need Help or Have Questions?**
- Contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Resources for Full-Time Tuition-Paid Texas Tech K-12 Students**

Full-time students enrolled in the tuition-paid program at Texas Tech K-12 have access to a variety of resources and supports:

**Academic Support:**
- **Certified Teachers:** Texas-certified teachers provide guidance, feedback, and personalized support throughout the academic year.
- **Academic Advisors and Counselors:** Available to help with course selection, academic planning, and career guidance.
- **Technical Support:** Assistance with technology-related issues is available.

**Learning Environment:**
- **Flexible, Self-Paced Online Learning:** Students can start courses at any time during the year and work at their own pace within a 180-day window for each course.
- **Wide Range of Courses:** Access to core subjects, electives, foreign languages, Advanced Placement (AP) courses, credit recovery, and acceleration options.

**Student Tools:**
- **Online Portal:** Manage courses, view grades, communicate with teachers, and access resources.
- **Canvas Learning Management System:** Used for course content, assignments, grades, and communication.
- **Proctorio Online Proctoring:** For secure online exams.

**Additional Resources:**
- **Office Hours:** Teachers host office hours for students to ask questions and receive additional help.
- **Student ID Cards:** Available for full-time students for identification and testing purposes.
- **Grade Reports and Transcripts:** Access to official grade reports and transcripts through the portal.

**Note:**
- Students in the tuition-paid program are responsible for purchasing their own textbooks and materials.
- There are no payment plans; full payment is required at enrollment.

**Contact for Support:**
- Phone: 1-800-692-6877
- Email: ttuk12@ttu.edu
